definition: In computational learning theory (machine learning and theory of computation), Rademacher complexity, named after Hans Rademacher, measures richness of a class of sets with respect to a probability distribution.
details: The concept can also be extended to real valued functions.

explainer.lead: Rademacher complexity measures how rich a class of sets is relative to a probability distribution, giving a way to reason about generalization in learning theory. It matters because such richness bounds help explain when a model can generalize rather than memorize.

tiers.eli5: It is a score for how many different patterns a set of rules can fit, given how the data is spread out.
tiers.practitioner: Theorists use it to bound generalization error for hypothesis classes under a distribution. A pitfall is that it depends on the distribution, so bounds can be loose or mismatched to real data.
tiers.paperLevel: A measure of the richness of a class of sets with respect to a probability distribution; the concept extends to real valued functions. Its bounds are tied to the assumed distribution.

explainer.example: A learning theorist compares the Rademacher complexity of two candidate function classes to judge which admits tighter generalization guarantees.
